To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supplementation with rice bran for 21 days in primiparous cows grazing native pastures reduced by 11 days postpartum anestrous period, without affecting body condition score and body weight of cows or their calves.

short-term supplementation with low-cost energy sources can reduce the length of post partum anestrus in primiparous cows, and that this effect is associated with increased insulin concentrations and reduced hepatic IGFBP2 expression.
supplementation with rice bran for 21 days postpartum decreased the length of post-partum anestrus in primiparous cows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of postpartum short-time supplementation on the metabolic, productive and reproductive performance in primiparous cows.

the effect of short-term nutritional supplementation on metabolic and productive responses, as well as hepatic gene expression associated with the reproductive responses of primiparous beef cattle in a grazing system.
the effects of a short-term postpartum supplementation on the endocrine-metabolic profile and hepatic gene transcription of primiparous beef cattle in grazing conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

supplementation with rice bran for 21 days postpartum improved reproductive performance in primiparous cows by increasing insulin sensitivity and decreasing hepatic expression of IGF binding protein 2, which may be related with the increase in the expression of the insulin receptor.
supplementation with rice bran for 21 days after calving did not affect productive and reproductive performance, but improved the metabolic status of cows in grazing conditions.

the supplementation with rice bran in grazing conditions, for a period of 21 days, improved reproductive performance of cows, associated with increased hepatic expression of IGF1, IGFBP2 and INSR mRNAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

supplementation with rice bran during 21 days postpartum reduced the length of post-partum anestrus in primiparous cows, which was associated with increased concentrations in blood glucose and insulin, reduced expression of IGFB2 mRNA in liver and increased expression of INSR mRNA in liver.

a short-term supplementation of cows with rice bran during the postpartum period in grazing conditions is effective in reducing the length of anestrus, and that this response is associated with increased glucose and insulin concentrations and reduced hepatic IGFBP2 gene expression.

a short-term supplementation of primiparous beef cattle in grazing conditions with rice bran can improve reproductive performance by modulating the metabolic and endocrine profile, and by modifying the hepatic gene expression of growth and insulin signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

short-term supplementation with a source of energy in the form of rice bran in primiparous cows grazing tropical pastures in a subtropical climate may be an effective strategy to improve their metabolic and reproductive performance.
supplementation with rice bran in grazing conditions for 21 days after calving is an efficient strategy to improve postpartum reproductive performance in primiparous cows.

short-term supplementation with 2 kg/cow/day of rice bran during 21 days after calving in primiparous cows grazing tropical native pastures reduced postpartum anovulation by 11 days, associated with increased glucose and insulin concentrations and reduced hepatic abundance of IGFBP-2 mRNA.
